To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

glutaryl-CoA-dehydrogenase (the enzyme deficient in GA1) is a component of multimeric dehydrogenase-complexes in the mitochondrial matrix and interacts with the mitochondrial proteins dihydrolipoyl S-succinlytransferase (the enzyme catalyzing the first step of lysine oxidation) and electron-transfer flavoprotein (the electron acceptor of glutaryl-Co-A-dehydrogenase)

the mitochondrial matrix enzyme GCDH is involved in the formation and/or maintenance of multimeric dehydrogenase enzyme complexes and that GCDH directly interacts with DLST and the β-subunits of the ETF complex.

we report here for first time on the interaction of glutaryl-Coa dehydrogenase with mitochondrial matrix proteins, which are involved in glutaryl-CoA formation, and the formation of the electron transfer chain, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the molecular interactions of GCDH with mitochondrial matrix proteins.
the elucidation of the biochemical mechanisms underlying the metabolic disorder glutaric aciduria type-1 (GA1).
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the pathogenesis of the neurometabolic disease GA1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GCDH forms a heterodimeric protein complex with DLST and that this complex is stabilized by the binding to ETFB.
the GA1 phenotype results from the combined effects of a number of factors.
GA1 patients are at risk of developing a potentially fatal metabolic disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GCDH forms a heteromeric complex with the DLST subunit of the branched chain α-keto acid dehydrogenase complex and the ETFB subunit of the ETF complex.
we have identified the first GCDH-interacting mitochondrial matrix proteins, DLST and ETFβ.
we have identified the first interacting partners for the GCDH protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GCDH forms homo- and possibly heteromeric complexes with DLST and/or ETFB.
we have identified the first interacting proteins of GCDH.
we identified for the first time the interaction of GCDH with other mitochondrial matrix proteins, which may provide new insights in the pathophysiology and treatment of GA1.
